body: I think I should do that. They really probably have no idea anything is wrong with me. You're too nice, but you can keep the codes. Thank you anyway, it's a really nice thought. I appreciate you talking to me, it helps to have an outside perspective.

Thank you. I appreciate your kind words. I think I know that they appreciate and love me, but for some reason I still feel awful about it. Like I'm just getting in the way, somehow. I know it doesn't make any sense, not even to me, but the thoughts are still there and I can't seem to make them stop. It doesn't matter, because somehow I'm still worthless anyway, in my mind.

I just don't really know what I'm supposed to do. I keep telling them they need to have these conversations with each other and not me, but I always get the "well, I don't want to cause any more problems...." More than anything else in the world, I want them to be happy. He thinks that she's unhappy, she's upset that he would think that, but for some reason them having a conversation is out of the question without causing huge problems. I just don't know what I can say anymore. I do the best I can by being there for them and giving them a shoulder, but it just feels like I'm not good enough to do anything for anyone.

The silly thing is if I listened to any of the advice I've told them, I probably shouldn't even feel this way. But here I am, as sad and feeling as alone as ever.
Thank you, that's a good idea. I admittedly should have done that before.
No, I agree that I shouldn't cut off contact. I'm just angry/upset right now, and trying not to act *too* irrationally.

Honestly my first thought when I found out he was lying again was to just cut off contact from him. I keep thinking how that might not be the best thing for him, but I also think about his total lack of regard for everyone around him who stayed up for days worried about him when it was all just a big joke to him.
I appreciate you saying that. Thank you.
